correctness.rationale: At a center z the pairs of neighbors with another common neighbor encode the squares through z; edge-disjointness makes them a matching. Any other neighbor subset of size >=2 contains a pair with unique common center z, so the descending-cardinality F < F∪{z} removals are genuine free-face collapses. The residual is G with a tetrahedral boundary on each square. One disk per square kills an edge-disjoint primitive cycle; the complementary disks attach trivially, giving (e-v+1-s) circles and s 2-spheres with torsion-free integral homology. Independently recreated the prescribed collapses for C4, C6 and a wedge of two squares, including all current free-face checks.
